questions.title: Can you say your ball is unplayable in a penalty area?
questions.question: Your ball lands in a penalty area, like near water or mud, and gets stuck behind rocks. Can you say it is unplayable and use the unplayable ball rule?

choices.text: Yes, you can always do that
No, you can't say it is unplayable in a penalty area
Only if another player says it's OK
Only if you cannot find the ball

questions.explanation: You are not allowed to say your ball is unplayable when it is in a penalty area. There are different rules for balls in penalty areas. You must use the penalty area rules to move your ball.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A place like a pond, stream, or muddy patch on the course that is marked with yellow or red lines or stakes.
When you decide you can’t hit the ball from where it is and want to take a penalty to move it, but you can't do this in a penalty area.

questions.teachingTip: You can only use the special penalty area drop rules when your ball is in a penalty area, not the unplayable ball rule.
likelyMisconceptions: Some children might think they can use the unplayable ball rule anywhere, even in a penalty area.
Kids may believe they need to ask other players before deciding.

questions.title: Declaring a ball unplayable in a penalty area
questions.question: Your ball is in a penalty area, stuck behind rocks. Are you allowed to declare it unplayable?

choices.text: No, you cannot declare it unplayable in a penalty area
Only if the ball is lost

questions.explanation: You cannot declare a ball unplayable in a penalty area. You must use the penalty area relief options instead.
